read_critical_collapse.gamma_value: The 2007 Living Review (arXiv:0711.4620) gives gamma only as "γ ≃ 0.37", on p.19 (page confirmed by cutting the parse). The 2025 update (arXiv:2507.07636) repeats "γ ≃ 0.37" on p.13 (page inferred). The precise value is γ = 0.374 ± 0.001, from the growing mode λ₁ = −2.674 ± 0.009 (Gundlach, gr-qc/9604019, abstract p.1). Simulations give γ_0 = 0.376 ± 0.003 and Δ_0 = 3.43 ± 0.05 (Olabarrieta et al., arXiv:0708.0513, Table III, p.5). Hod–Piran measure β ≈ 0.37. Echoing period: "∆ ≃ 3.44" from numerical evolutions and "∆ = 3.445452402(3)" from the constructed solution (0711.4620 p.14; 2507.07636 p.10). The wiggle comes from Eq.(11), p.8 of 0711.4620: ln M = γ ln(p−p*) + c + f(γ ln(p−p*) + c), "where f (z) has period ∆". For the scalar field, the period actually seen in ln(p−p*) is Δ/(2γ) ≈ 4.61 (gr-qc/9604019 p.13). Hod–Piran measured "≈ 4.6" (gr-qc/9606087 pp.1–2). Validation target: γ ≈ 0.374, Δ ≈ 3.4455, wiggle period in ln(p−p*) ≈ 4.61.
read_critical_collapse.equations_summary:
Normalization, Choptuik/Gundlach form: G = c = 1 (2507.07636 p.3). The field equations are G_ab = 8π(∇_aφ∇_bφ − ½ g_ab ∇_cφ∇^cφ) and ∇_a∇^aφ = 0 (0711.4620 Eqs.18–19, p.12; 2507.07636 Eqs.25–26, p.9).

Metric: ds² = −α²dt² + a²dr² + r²dΩ² (Eq.20, p.12). The lapse is fixed by α = 1 at r = 0, so t is central proper time (p.13).

Variables: Φ = φ_,r and Π = (a/α)φ_,t (Eq.21, p.13).

Evolution:
- Φ_,t = ((α/a)Π)_,r
- Π_,t = r⁻²(r²(α/a)Φ)_,r
(Eq.22, p.13; 2025 Eqs.29–30, p.9)

Hamiltonian constraint: a_,r/a + (a²−1)/(2r) = 2πr(Π²+Φ²) (Eq.23).

Slicing condition: α_,r/α − a_,r/a − (a²−1)/r = 0 (Eq.24).

Momentum constraint: a_,t/α = 4πrΦΠ (Eq.25). It is redundant in the fully constrained scheme (p.13; 2025 Eqs.31–33, p.9).

The 2π vs 4π factors: 2π multiplies Π²+Φ² in the Hamiltonian constraint and 4π multiplies ΦΠ in the momentum constraint. Both follow from G_ab = 8πT_ab with T_ab carrying no 1/(4π). Substituting (23) into (24) gives α_,r/α = 2πr(Π²+Φ²) + (a²−1)/(2r). That is my algebra; neither source prints it.

Mass function: M(t,r) = (r/2)(1 − 1/a²) (Olabarrieta et al. Eq.20, p.3). It is purely geometric, so it holds in either field normalization. It equals the ADM mass as r→∞, and 2M/r → 1 signals horizon formation.

Olabarrieta et al. use a rescaled field. At l=0 their Eqs.(17)–(19), p.3, read:
- (1/a)a_r = (r/2)(Π²+Φ²) − (a²−1)/(2r)
- (1/α)α_r = (r/2)(Π²+Φ²) + (a²−1)/(2r)
- a_t = rαΠΦ
Comparing with Gundlach's Eq.(23) gives ψ_Olabarrieta = √(4π) φ_Choptuik. That is my derived comparison, not stated in the paper. They normalize the lapse with α(t,r_max)a(t,r_max) = 1 (Eq.27, p.3) and analyze in central proper time. Regularity conditions are a(t,0) = 1 and ∂_r a = ∂_r α = 0 at r = 0 (Eqs.21–23, p.3).

Gundlach 1997 (gr-qc/9604019) keeps G explicit: 8πG, with X = √(2πG)(r/a)φ_,r.
read_critical_collapse.caveats:
1. How pages were pinned. These were confirmed by cutting the arXiv PDF parse at a set page count (Firecrawl maxPages):
   - 0711.4620: pp. 2, 8, 12, 13, 14, 19
   - 2507.07636: p.6
   - gr-qc/9604019: p.13
   - 0708.0513: pp.2 and 5
   
   These were inferred from the table of contents plus parse page breaks and are flagged as such:
   - 2507.07636: pp. 3, 9, 10, 13, 16
   - 0708.0513: p.3
   
   These were not pinned:
   - the λ₁ quote, p.11 or 12
   - the apparent-horizon (AH) mass passage of 0711.4620, p.16 or 17
   - Hod–Piran Eq.9, p.≥3
   - Marsa–Choptuik, no page

2. Math in the quotes is the parser's LaTeX rendering of the PDF, not raw glyphs. The PDF parse of Olabarrieta Eqs.(17)–(18) was garbled, so the equation text is taken from the arXiv HTML of the same v1. The page comes from the PDF.

3. The wiggle period is easy to get wrong. GM2007 Eq.(11) says f has period Δ in z = γ ln(p−p*)+c, which would give 9.2 in ln(p−p*). For the real scalar field the critical solution is symmetric under φ→−φ, so the geometric quantities echo with Δ/2 (Olabarrieta p.5). The observable wiggle in ln(p−p*) therefore has period Δ/(2γ) ≈ 4.61 (Gundlach 1997 p.13). Hod–Piran write ϖ = Δ/β ≈ 4.6, which does not match their own numbers: 3.44/0.37 ≈ 9.3. Their measured 4.6 matches Δ/(2γ). Test the code for ≈4.61, not 9.2.

4. What counts as the black-hole mass:
   - The mass function f_M depends on the slicing and can jump once per period (2507.07636 p.10). The curvature scaling of R_max, Eq.(18) on p.6, is gauge-independent and the cleaner check.
   - A polar-areal code cannot penetrate the apparent horizon (Olabarrieta p.3). So its "mass" is the AH/MOTS mass where 2M/r → 1, and later infall can raise the true mass (0711.4620 pp.16–17).
   - Choptuik's scaling held from 10⁻⁶ up to 0.9 of the ADM mass, with p* tuned to 10⁻¹⁵ (0711.4620 pp.13–14; Olabarrieta p.5).

5. Olabarrieta p.3 says polar slicing "can be derived from the demand that Tr(K_ab)=K^r_r+K^θ_θ+K^φ_φ=K^r_r+2K^θ_θ=0". As printed, that reads as maximal slicing. Polar slicing is conventionally K^θ_θ = 0; this is my own knowledge, not quoted. Implement from Eq.(18)/(24), not from that sentence.

6. Item 3 (Schwarzschild exterior, surface gravity 1/(4M)): none found. No fetched source says that the black hole formed in Einstein–massless-scalar collapse is Schwarzschild outside the matter, non-extremal, or has surface gravity 1/(4M). The nearest statements are:
   - Olabarrieta p.3: the mass aspect measures the enclosed mass in vacuum regions, and polar-areal coordinates behave like Schwarzschild coordinates.
   - Marsa–Choptuik: Schwarzschild forms hold in vacuum regions; page not pinned.
   - 2507.07636 p.16: the end state is Schwarzschild for Einstein–Yang–Mills, a different matter model.

read_braneworld_collapse.gamma_value:
The board's eq. (17) is exactly the zero-temperature (extremal) member of Casadio-Fabbri-Mazzacurati Case I, with PPN parameters beta = gamma = 5/4. Equivalently eta = 3(beta - 1) = 3/4 and eta-bar = (4/9)eta = 1/3. I derived this; it is not stated in any paper.

The steps:
- CFM eq. (8) gives H = 1/A = (1 - 2M/r)(1 - (4 beta - 1)M/(2r)) / (1 - 3M/(2r)).
- Setting 4 beta - 1 = 4 gives H = (1 - 2m/r)^2 / (1 - 3m/(2r)).
- CFM eq. (13) gives T_H = sqrt(1 - 3 eta-bar)/(8 pi M) = 0 at eta-bar = 1/3, which is the member CFM single out on p. 4 as 'completely regular'.
- Their turning surface r0 = (3/2)M(1 + eta-bar) = 2M then coincides with the horizon r_h = 2M.
- The same metric is Germani-Maartens's second exterior, eqs. (42)-(43), with C/lambda = -N/2 (G = 1).

I checked both identities exactly with rational arithmetic at several radii.
read_braneworld_collapse.equations_summary:
FORMULATION (Wang and Choptuik 2016 PRL; Wang thesis 2015)
- Bulk: 5D Einstein equations with Lambda < 0. Background ds^2 = (l^2/z^2)(eta_ab dx^a dx^b + dz^2) with z >= l and the brane at z = l. The domain is one-sided, so Z2 is built in.
- Variables depend on (t, r, z) once spherical symmetry is imposed on the brane, which makes the bulk axisymmetric.
- Compactified grid coordinates: R^ = r/(r + r0) and Z^ = (z - l)/(z - l + z0), uniform in both.
- Conformal metric g~ = Psi^-2 g with Psi = l/z (q = 2). The extra Psi terms are treated as matter, so the conformal problem is asymptotically flat. Units: l = k5 = 1.
- Generalized harmonic gauge with regularized Cartesian-component variables:
  - metric components eta~_tt, eta~_tr, eta~_rr, eta~_tz, eta~_rz, eta~_zz, plus W with eta~_thth = eta~_rr + rW;
  - source functions H~_mu = h~_mu + (2/r)(eta~_{mu r}/eta~_thth).
- Axis conditions: eta~_{tt,r} = eta~_{rr,r} = eta~_{zz,r} = eta~_{tz,r} = eta~_tr = eta~_rz = W = 0.

BRANE
- Israel junction: K+ = -K- = (1/2) k_d (lambda h/(d-2) + tau - h tau/(d-2)). It gives Neumann-type conditions on eta~_{tt,z}, eta~_{tr,z}, eta~_{rr,z}, W_z (explicit forms not printed).
- The GH constraints are imposed exactly at the brane. They fix eta~_{tz,z}, eta~_{rz,z}, eta~_{zz,z}.
- The perpendicular gauge eta~_tz = eta~_rz = 0 at z = l is enforced by writing eta~_tz = (z - l) xi_t and eta~_rz = (z - l) xi_r. This keeps the apparent horizon smooth and perpendicular at the brane.
- Brane matter obeys D_a D^a Phi = 0 with the induced metric and enters only through tau_ab in the junction condition.
- Effective brane equation: G_ab = -Lambda4 h_ab + k4 tau_ab + k5^2 pi_ab - E_ab. The thesis says only that E 'is only important at high energy regime'.

INITIAL DATA
- Time-symmetric, with spatial metric (l^2/z^2)[e^(2A+2B)(dr^2 + dz^2) + e^(2A-2B) r^2 dOmega^2].
- Junction conditions: A_z = 1 - e^(A+B) - (1/6)e^(-A-B)Phi_r^2 and B_z = -(1/4)e^(-A-B)Phi_r^2. At least two free metric functions are needed.
- The evolution-ready ansatz (4.26) adds a lapse e^(2a) and g_zz = e^(2b), with a_z = (1/12)e^(-2A-2B)Phi_r^2 and b_z = -(h~_z + ...).
- Scalar field: Phi(0, r) = A0 exp[-(r - x0)^2/sigma_r^2].

GAUGE AND NUMERICS
- Gauges: harmonic h~ = 0; Pretorius lapse driver (5.20) with alpha0 = 1; damped wave (5.21). Damped wave was used for small holes, the lapse driver for large ones.
- Constraint damping Z~_mu nu = kappa(n_(mu C_nu) - (1+p)/2 g n.C). A brane-enhanced variant with F = z^4/(z^4 - 0.99) was superseded by imposing the constraints exactly at the brane.
- Second-order central differences, fourth-order Kreiss-Oliger dissipation, Courant factor 0.5, Newton-Gauss-Seidel update.
- Convergence tests at dR^ = dZ^ = 1/256 and 1/512 on 16 CPUs. The black-hole runs were single-CPU on a uniform grid with no AMR.
- Apparent horizon found by ODE shooting, then excised with one-sided dissipation.

RESULTS
- Weak data disperse; strong data form an apparent horizon of finite bulk extent. Example: first horizon at t = 2.3, settled by t ~ 5.5, last at t = 6.1, giving r_a = 0.61 l.
- Sizes 0.04 l to 19.6 l. Small holes approach 5D Schwarzschild: A_bulk = 2 pi^2 r_a^3 and C5 = 2 pi r_a.
- Large holes approach the black-string area law, with C5 ~ 4 log(zeta r_a): zeta = 2.71 here against 2.8 from Figueras-Wiseman.
- The final states are only 'apparently stationary' and the evolution eventually departs. No late-time brane metric functions (g_tt, g_rr) are reported.

WEYL-CHARGED BRANE METRICS IN THE BULK (static y-extensions only)
- CRSS: Gaussian normal coordinates (N = 1), free evolution in chi with Crank-Nicholson. For tidal RN, K diverges at a finite chi_crit for all beta != 0.
- CM: multipole (1/r) expansion with df_n/dz(0) = -sigma f_n(0) to order 19. For eta < 0 the horizon closes as a 'pancake'; for eta > 0 constant-r geodesics form caustics.
- Board's eq. (17): F = 1 - 2m/r and H = (1 - 2m/r)^2/(1 - 3m/(2r)), which is CFM Case I at eta-bar = 1/3 (T_H = 0, r0 = r_h = 2m).
read_braneworld_collapse.caveats:
1. Pagination.
- Wang-Choptuik pages are those of the 5-page arXiv v2 PDF; the mapping to PRL 117, 011102 journal pages was not confirmed.
- Thesis pages are given as the PDF page with the printed page in brackets.
- Emparan et al. pages are the journal/arXiv footer numbers.
- Choptuik's slide numbers could not be confirmed: the scrape dropped them.

2. Quote fidelity.
- Text came from PDF extraction (alphaXiv page-tagged text). Line-break hyphens were rejoined and math was transcribed to ASCII.
- The Dadhich et al. extraction had lost ligatures (e.g. 'eective'); these were restored.
- Wording is otherwise verbatim, including the authors' own grammar ('In ours simulations', 'atrophysical').

3. Coverage of the thesis.
- I read targeted sections by query, not all 180 pages.
- The production grid size of the black-hole runs (as opposed to the 1/256 and 1/512 convergence grids) was not found. The only stated controls are r0 = z0 compactification and unigrid on one CPU; no AMR was used in any black-hole run.

4. Internal inconsistencies.
- The thesis (printed p. 116) says that after horizon formation 'we gradually change the gauge into (3) to drive the value of alpha toward alpha0 = 1'. Option (3) is the damped wave gauge, but that description fits (2), the lapse driver. The slides say 'Always blend to lapse driver'.
- The PRL and thesis label the five initial-data families differently: PRL (iv) is (x0, sigma_r) = (0, 0.3), while thesis Fig. 5.12 has (ii) = (0, 0.3).
- The thesis gives r_a in (0.04 l, 19.6 l), but Table 5.1 tops out at 15.1 and Fig. 5.12 spans about 0.04 to 15 l.
- The slides say 'stable, static black hole solutions'; the paper and thesis claim only 'apparently stationary' states that the evolution 'inevitably departs from', with no slicing adapted to the Killing vector.

5. What Wang-Choptuik do not provide.
- No explicit late-time brane metric functions. They report only r_a, A_bulk, C5 and brane ADM/Hawking 'energies'.
- No statement on bulk curvature singularities beyond excision and the remark that coordinate or physical singularities crash the code.
- No charged, extremal, rotating or Weyl-charged brane configurations. So there is no dynamical test of tidal RN or CFM-type end states, and no comparison of the late-time brane metric with eq. (17).

6. Follow-ups.
- An INSPIRE 'refersto' query listed 21 records citing the PRL.
- The only time-evolution follow-up found is Emparan et al. 2023. It is a large-D effective theory with Karch-Randall (AdS) branes in global AdS, not full GR, and not an RS2 flat brane; the authors note that brane gravity there is closer to D-dimensional.
- No full-GR dynamical follow-up of Wang-Choptuik was found. The search was not exhaustive.

7. Extremal and Weyl-term literature is all static.
- CRSS and Casadio-Mazzacurati extend brane metrics in the extra coordinate; they do not evolve in time.
- CRSS's ansatz has g_tt = -1/g_rr, so it cannot represent eq. (17), which has F != H.
- Casadio-Mazzacurati's quantitative results assume |eta| << 1 and M sigma >> 1. The board's member has eta = 3/4 > 0, and their eta > 0 remark (caustics, Gaussian normal coordinates not covering the bulk) is only qualitative there.
- CFM themselves leave the bulk extension of Case I open.

8. Derived claims are mine.
- The identification of eq. (17) with CFM Case I at beta = gamma = 5/4 (eta-bar = 1/3, T_H = 0) is my algebra, checked exactly. The extremal member itself is named in CFM p. 4.
- So is the equivalence with Germani-Maartens's exterior at C/lambda = -N/2. Their matched stellar value of C is positive for R > 3GM/2, so eq. (17) is not the exterior of their uniform-density star.

9. Bruni-Germani-Maartens rest on assumptions.
- Their 'non-static exterior' theorem assumes Oppenheimer-Snyder homogeneous dust and standard 4D matching.
- 'Transient, tends to Schwarzschild at large distance' is their expectation, not a computation.
